title: Black Jack vs Latex-ite Driveway Sealer: Which Pail to Buy
h1: Black Jack vs Latex-ite Driveway Sealer
query: black jack vs latex-ite driveway sealer
description: Pick Latex-ite Ultra Shield for more coverage (400-500 sq ft a pail) and 40°F cures; pick Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 for a heavy, rubberized coat.
dek: Pick Latex-ite Ultra Shield for more coverage (400-500 sq ft a pail) and 40°F cures; pick Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 for a heavy, rubberized coat.
intro: Two water-based brands share the same aisle and the same pail size. The labels differ more than the pails look: coverage, cold-weather limits and the year claims are not the same.

For most driveways, Latex-ite Ultra Shield is the better buy: its label lists 400 to 500 square feet per pail on smooth asphalt against 350 for Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000, and it cures down to 40°F. Black Jack wins on a worn, open-textured surface where you want a heavy rubberized coat. The age of your asphalt, the weather window and what your local store stocks change the answer, and this page covers each one.

quickAnswer: Pick Black Jack if your blacktop is gray, rough and open-textured, you want the heaviest rubberized, urethane-enhanced pail on the shelf, or your store only stocks the Drive-Maxx line. Pick Latex-ite if you want more square feet per pail on the label, a cure rating down to 40°F for a late-season job, or a 10-year warranty from the Ultra Shield tier. On a smooth, sound driveway that was sealed two or three years ago, the two flagship pails are close enough that prep and weather will decide the result, not the logo.

sections.h: Which Is Better, Black Jack 1000 or Latex-ite Ultra Shield?

blocks.p: Latex-ite Ultra Shield is the better choice for most homeowners, and Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 is the better choice for a tired driveway that needs filling as much as sealing. Both are their brands' top retail tier, both are water-based asphalt emulsions in 4.75-gallon pails, and both claim ten years. The differences are in the fine print: spread per pail, cure temperature and what each is built to do.

Black Jack's data sheet calls Drive-Maxx 1000 its best-quality rubberized blacktop filler and sealer. It is latex-polymer enhanced, carries sand particles to fill small cracks, and is described as urethane enhanced for longest life and as a heavy vehicle formula. That recipe builds a thick, dark film, which is why the label coverage is a modest 350 square feet per coat on smooth asphalt and 300 on rough or worn asphalt. You are paying for solids that stay on the surface, which is exactly what a gray, stony driveway needs.

Latex-ite describes Ultra Shield as a filler sealer with a flexible polymer system, an EZ-Gel formula, UV protection and a non-skid finish, and it is labeled low VOC, coal tar free and PAH compliant. Its product page lists 400 to 500 square feet per pail per coat on smooth or previously sealed asphalt and 300 to 400 on rough, porous or never-sealed surfaces. On a driveway that was sealed a few years ago, that can mean one fewer pail per coat than the Black Jack flagship. Latex-ite also says its ThermaSeal technology lets the coat cure down to 40°F.

So the decision is mostly about the surface. If you can see the stones and the fine material between them has washed out, a heavier pail like Drive-Maxx 1000 lays down more body per square foot, and that is where it earns its higher price. If the surface is still tight and black underneath the fade, Ultra Shield's wider spread saves money and its cooler cure rating gives you more days on the calendar. Our [Latex-ite driveway sealer review](/latex-ite-driveway-sealer-review/) goes deeper on the Latex-ite side, and the [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) place both pails against the rest of the market.
THE RULE
Match the pail to the texture, not the year on the label.

Rough, open asphalt wants the heavier fill of Drive-Maxx 1000. Smooth, previously sealed asphalt gets more square feet per dollar from Ultra Shield. Both labels require clean, dry pavement and two thin coats to deliver what they promise.

sections.h: What Are the Black Jack Drive-Maxx and Latex-ite Product Tiers?

blocks.p: Black Jack sells five Drive-Maxx tiers and Latex-ite sells four blacktop sealers, according to the two makers' own product pages checked on November 18, 2026. Black Jack's numbering is simple: the number divided by 100 is the year claim printed on the product page, from Drive-Maxx 200 (2 year) up to Drive-Maxx 1000 (10 year). Latex-ite names its tiers instead, and its year figures are stated as warranties on the product pages.

blocks.p: Latex-ite Airport Grade is the name many shoppers still search for, and the current version on the maker's site is Airport Grade+, a polymer-fortified filler sealer with a 5-year warranty and the same 400-500 and 300-400 square foot coverage ranges as Ultra Shield. A Latex-ite Pro-Grade sealer does not appear in the maker's current blacktop lineup, and the Optimum Pro resurfacer is listed as discontinued by at least one retailer. If you find either on a shelf, read the pail's own label rather than assuming it matches a current product.

Black Jack's lineup has also been renamed: product pages for older Drive-Kote, Drive-Seal and New Black pails now point to Drive-Maxx numbers, so store listings still mix the names. For either brand, buy by tier, read the coverage and year claim on the actual pail, and buy every pail for one job from the same tier and batch code, which Black Jack's data sheet recommends to avoid color shading.

Latex-ite Acrylic Grade is the odd one out: an acrylic in a 3.4-gallon pail that the maker says must be rolled on, with car traffic claimed in four hours. If you are weighing chemistries rather than brands, our [oil-based vs water-based driveway sealer](/oil-based-vs-water-based-driveway-sealer/) comparison explains where each family fits.

sections.h: Black Jack Drive-Maxx 500 Review: Is the Mid-Tier Pail Worth It?

blocks.p: Black Jack Drive-Maxx 500 is a reasonable mid-tier pail for a sound driveway sealed on a regular schedule, but it has a narrower weather window than the flagship. Black Jack lists it as a 5-year blacktop filler and sealer at $29.99, with an E-Z stir, latex-enhanced formula. Its data sheet gives the same coverage as Drive-Maxx 1000, 350 square feet per coat on smooth asphalt and 300 on rough or worn asphalt, so you do not save pails by stepping down, only dollars per pail.

The important difference is temperature. The Drive-Maxx 500 data sheet says air temperature must be 55°F and rising and below 90°F during application, with no rain or overnight lows below 50°F expected within 36 hours. Drive-Maxx 1000 is rated to 45°F. In practice that means the 500 is a summer pail, and a September or early-spring job in the northern states is a better fit for the flagship or for Latex-ite Ultra Shield. The 500 also lists slower foot traffic, about 2 to 4 hours, with 24 to 48 hours before vehicles.

The 5-year figure deserves a careful read. The data sheet's warranty language covers the product against defects for five years from the date of purchase; it is not a promise that one application will look fresh for five years on your driveway. Owners commonly report that mid-tier emulsions need a refresh every two to three years on a driveway with daily traffic, with turning areas and shaded sections wearing first. Plan your budget on that cycle and treat any extra year as a bonus.

Buy Drive-Maxx 500 for a smooth driveway in decent shape, sealed in midsummer, on a two-to-three-year cycle. Skip it for cool-weather jobs, for rough, stony asphalt that wants the heavier 700 or 1000, or if Latex-ite Airport Grade+ costs about the same at your store, since its label lists wider coverage on smooth asphalt.

sections.h: Which Covers More per Pail, and How Long Does Each Last?

blocks.p: Latex-ite covers more per pail on paper, and neither brand's year number tells you how long a coat will last on your driveway. Latex-ite lists 400 to 500 square feet per 4.75-gallon pail per coat on smooth or previously sealed asphalt for both Ultra Shield and Airport Grade+, and 300 to 400 on rough, porous or never-sealed asphalt. Black Jack's data sheets list 350 square feet on smooth and 300 on rough or worn asphalt for Drive-Maxx 500 and 1000. Both makers add that coverage depends on the condition of the existing surface.

Run the numbers for a typical 600 square foot single-car driveway that needs two coats, or 1,200 square feet of spreading. On rough asphalt, Black Jack's 300-square-foot figure works out to four pails, and Latex-ite's 300 to 400 range works out to three or four. On smooth, previously sealed asphalt, Black Jack still needs about four pails, while Latex-ite's 400 to 500 range needs three. Very thirsty, oxidized driveways often drink more than any label suggests, so buy one spare pail you can return unopened; our sibling pages plan on 250 to 350 square feet a pail for older, porous blacktop for exactly that reason.

Durability is where the marketing gets ahead of the driveway. Black Jack prints 2, 3, 5, 7 and 10 years on its tiers, and Latex-ite states 2-year, 5-year and 10-year warranties. These are tier names and warranty periods, and both makers attach conditions: Latex-ite says its warranty is honored only when any repair products used were Latex-ite products and voids it for roller application, and Black Jack's data sheet makes two thin coats a requirement and points to its own warranty terms. Read the warranty terms on the maker's site before you count on one.

Owners commonly report about two to three years from a well-applied two-coat job with either brand, longer in full sun and shorter in shade or where a plow scrapes, which matches our [asphalt sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/). Premium tiers tend to hold color and resist scuffs longer, but no pail in this aisle turns a two-year job into a ten-year one.

sections.h: Which Dries Faster and Works in Cooler Weather?

blocks.p: The two flagships dry about equally fast, and Latex-ite Ultra Shield has the lower cold limit. Black Jack says Drive-Maxx 1000 is ready for light foot traffic in about one hour under good drying conditions, which it defines as temperatures above 75°F, clear skies and humidity below 35 percent, and that vehicles must wait a minimum of 24 hours; its application notes give 24 to 48 hours. Latex-ite says Ultra Shield is foot-traffic ready in one hour. Its product page does not state a vehicle time, so allow the same day or two.

Cold-weather ratings differ more. Latex-ite rates Ultra Shield to cure down to 40°F. Black Jack rates Drive-Maxx 1000 for application from 45°F to 99°F and says not to apply if rain or overnight lows below 45°F are expected within 36 hours. The mid tiers are stricter: Latex-ite asks for at least 55°F at night for Airport Grade+ and warns against sealing in early spring or late fall, and Black Jack wants 55°F and rising for Drive-Maxx 500 with overnight lows above 50°F.

A low rating is a minimum, not a target. Every emulsion cures faster and harder in warm sun, so a 40°F rating is most useful for squeezing in a job in late September, not for planning one in November. Black Jack also asks you to apply onto a slightly damp, not wet, surface after rinsing and to put the second coat on perpendicular to the first once the first has cured, roughly two to four hours later. Our step-by-step guide on [how to seal a driveway](/how-to-seal-a-driveway/) covers the full sequence from cleaning to the second coat.

sections.h: How Much Do Black Jack and Latex-ite Cost, and Where Are They Sold?

blocks.p: Black Jack publishes list prices from $19.99 for Drive-Maxx 200 to $44.99 for Drive-Maxx 1000 on its own site, checked November 18, 2026. Latex-ite does not publish prices on its product pages, so its pails are priced by each retailer. In stores, the two brands usually sit in the same price bands tier for tier: entry pails near the bottom of the aisle, mid tiers in the middle and the 10-year flagships at the top. Shelf prices move through the season and between regions, so compare on the day.

Compare cost per square foot, not per pail. A pail that costs a few dollars more but spreads 450 square feet instead of 350 is the cheaper job. On rough asphalt the gap narrows, because both brands drop to about 300 square feet per coat.

Where you can buy them matters, because you want every pail from one store and one batch. Black Jack Drive-Maxx pails are listed at Home Depot, Ace Hardware, Tractor Supply and Canadian Tire, among others. Latex-ite pails are listed at Home Depot, Ace Hardware, Do it Best stores and Tractor Supply, and Henry sells Airport Grade in Canada. Stock is seasonal: shelves fill in spring and thin out by early fall. Our [Home Depot driveway sealer guide](/driveway-sealer-home-depot/) lists what that chain typically carries and how many pails common driveway sizes need.

sections.h: What Do Consumer Reports and Owner Reviews Say About Black Jack and Latex-ite?

blocks.p: We could not verify a current Consumer Reports result for these exact pails, so this page does not quote one. Consumer Reports runs its own lab evaluations and publishes ratings to its members; any ranking it gives Black Jack or Latex-ite is its work, not ours, and its scores may cover older formulas than the ones now on shelves. If you subscribe, check the date of the rating and the exact product name, since both brands have renamed tiers several times.

Owner reviews on retailer sites follow the same pattern for both brands. The common praise is appearance: a deep, even black that makes an old driveway look new for the first season, with Black Jack's flagship often singled out for its dark finish. The common complaints are coverage below the label on old, porous asphalt, the effort of stirring a heavy pail, and peeling where the surface was dirty, damp or sealed too thick. Those show up under both logos, which says more about prep than brand. Comparisons that crown a clear winner often quietly pit one brand's entry pail against the other's flagship, so check the tiers.

sections.h: Is Either One an Epoxy Asphalt Sealer, and What Is the Best Brand of Driveway Sealer?

blocks.p: Neither Black Jack nor Latex-ite sells an epoxy driveway sealer; both make water-based asphalt emulsions modified with latex, rubber or polymer, plus one acrylic pail from Latex-ite. The best-known epoxy-branded option in the same aisle is Rust-Oleum EpoxyShield Blacktop, which is a different product family. Shoppers searching for epoxy asphalt sealer brands usually want a harder, more chemical-resistant finish, and on a home driveway the practical options are a premium polymer emulsion, an acrylic, or a contractor-applied sealcoat.

There is no single best brand of driveway sealer, but there is a best tier for each driveway. For most homeowners with sound asphalt, a polymer-modified filler sealer from a major brand, applied in two thin coats in warm weather, is the right buy. Our [asphalt driveway sealer rankings](/best-asphalt-driveway-sealer-reviews/) put Latex-ite Airport Grade first for most drives and Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 as the premium-finish pick, and this comparison agrees: Latex-ite for value and cooler weather, Black Jack for a heavy coat on worn asphalt.

Safety is similar for both. Both are water-based and clean up with soap and water while wet, and Latex-ite labels its blacktop sealers coal tar free and PAH compliant. Black Jack's data sheet still calls for protective clothing and eyewear because the product can irritate skin, and asks you to transport pails upright in the cargo area, never on a passenger seat. Wear gloves and safety glasses, keep children and pets off the drive until it cures, and never pour leftover sealer into a storm drain. If you are offered a solvent-based or coal tar sealer instead, read our [oil vs water-based comparison](/oil-based-vs-water-based-driveway-sealer/) first, since those need more ventilation and are banned in some states and cities.

mistakes: Comparing pail prices instead of cost per square foot

A Black Jack pail lists 350 square feet per coat on smooth asphalt and a Latex-ite Ultra Shield pail lists 400 to 500. The cheaper pail can be the more expensive driveway. Divide the price by the label coverage for your surface before deciding.
Reading the year on the pail as a promise

The 5, 7 and 10 on these pails are tier names and warranty periods with conditions attached. Owners commonly report two to three years between coats on a busy driveway. Budget on that cycle and treat anything longer as a bonus.
Mixing brands or tiers on one job

Black Jack's data sheet says not to blend its sealer with other driveway products and to match batch codes across pails. Buy every pail for one job from the same brand, tier and batch so the finish does not shade from one section to the next.
Using another brand's crack filler and expecting the warranty

Latex-ite says its warranty is honored only if any repair products used were Latex-ite products, and Black Jack points owners to its own crack fillers. If the warranty matters to you, fill cracks with the same brand as the sealer and keep the receipts.
Sealing a mid-tier pail in cool weather

Drive-Maxx 500 and Airport Grade+ both want overnight temperatures in the 50s. Applying them in a cold snap leaves a soft coat that tracks and wears early. In shoulder seasons, use a flagship rated to 40-45°F or wait for warmer nights.
bottomLine: Latex-ite Ultra Shield is the better buy for most driveways: its label lists more square feet per pail on smooth asphalt, it is rated to cure down to 40°F, and it carries a 10-year warranty. Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 is the better buy for a gray, rough driveway that needs a heavy rubberized coat, and Black Jack's five numbered tiers make it easy to match price to expectations. Whichever logo you choose, buy by tier and by texture, compare cost per square foot, match every pail's batch, fill cracks with the same brand's product, and spread two thin coats in warm, dry weather. Plan to reseal every two to three years, whatever the pail promises.

faqs.q: How does Latex-ite compare to Black Jack sealant?
faqs.a: Tier for tier, they are close. Both sell water-based asphalt emulsions in 4.75-gallon pails with 2-, 5- and 10-year tiers. Latex-ite's labels list more coverage on smooth asphalt, 400 to 500 square feet per pail against 350, and its Ultra Shield cures down to 40°F. Black Jack's Drive-Maxx 1000 is a heavier rubberized, urethane-enhanced pail suited to rough, worn surfaces.

faqs.q: Is Black Jack Drive-Maxx 1000 better than Latex-ite Ultra Shield?
faqs.a: Not for every driveway. Drive-Maxx 1000 is the better pick on a gray, stony surface that needs filling, because its heavy body lays down more material per square foot. Ultra Shield is the better pick on smooth or previously sealed asphalt, where its wider label coverage saves a pail per coat, and in cool weather, since it is rated to cure at 40°F.

faqs.q: Has Consumer Reports rated Black Jack vs Latex-ite?
faqs.a: Consumer Reports publishes its own ratings to members, and we could not verify a current result for these exact pails, so we do not quote one. If you check, confirm the rating date and the exact tier name, because both brands have renamed products and an older rating may cover a formula that is no longer sold.

faqs.q: Is Black Jack Drive-Maxx 500 worth buying?
faqs.a: It is a fair mid-tier pail for a smooth driveway sealed in midsummer. Black Jack lists it at $29.99 with a 5-year claim and the same 350 and 300 square foot coverage as the flagship. Its data sheet requires 55°F and rising and overnight lows above 50°F, so it is a poor fit for spring or fall jobs.

faqs.q: Can I put Latex-ite over an old Black Jack coat?
faqs.a: Generally yes, once the old coat is fully cured, clean and well bonded, because both are water-based asphalt emulsions. Do not mix the two in a pail. Pressure wash, degrease oil spots, let the surface dry, and follow the new pail's label. Peeling or flaking old sealer should be scraped and swept off first, or the new coat will fail with it.

faqs.q: Can I apply Black Jack or Latex-ite with a roller?
faqs.a: Use a squeegee for both flagship lines. Black Jack says a squeegee must be used to spread the product at the right rate, and Latex-ite says a roller is the wrong applicator for Ultra Shield and voids the warranty. The exception is Latex-ite Acrylic Grade, which the maker says must be rolled on.

faqs.q: Are Black Jack and Latex-ite coal tar sealers?
faqs.a: The current lines covered here are water-based asphalt emulsions, not coal tar. Latex-ite labels Ultra Shield, Airport Grade+ and Dura Sand Mix coal tar free and PAH compliant. Coal tar sealers are banned in several states and cities. Check the label on the exact pail you buy, and wear gloves and eye protection either way.
